sonnet.problem: This story card only repeats the date from verse 2, which the previous choice card just covered, and adds nothing new from the passage. It is mainly a joke, so it does not move the baker forward.
sonnet.rule: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

sonnet.problem: This card re-asks the point of card 12. Verse 7 says she poured the blood on the bare rock and did not cover it with dust on the ground. Card 12 already asked where the blood was poured, so this is one fact asked twice.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question. An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The question says "With the fire roaring like that." Verse 10 says to pile on logs and kindle the fire, but it never says the fire roars. This is an exaggeration in Papa Dorin's narration.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The statement joins two claims: the pot "has frustrated every effort so far" and "even the fire has removed its thick rust." The first is true and the second is false, so the baker cannot mark it cleanly. "So far" is also added to the text.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.
